Market Friction

The Three Fatal Bottlenecks for African Founders

Why starting and scaling an enterprise today is needlessly painful

03 / 12
01

Regulatory Drag

Registering with CAC, obtaining Tax ID (TIN), opening a corporate bank account, and securing sector licenses (SCUML, Money Lender, Trademarks) takes up to 8 weeks through corrupt manual agents.

6+ Wks
Average manual timeline to achieve full legal & banking readiness in Nigeria.
02

Distribution Void

Builders have zero organic audience. Traditional PR agencies demand ₦1.5M to ₦3M monthly retainers with zero guarantees. Product Hunt yields zero African local payment adoption.

88%
Of African apps have fewer than 100 monthly active users post-launch due to zero distribution.
03

Capital Asymmetry

Venture capital and institutional media are hyper-clustered in Lagos. Thriving industrial innovators, agribusiness leaders, and software engineers in Port Harcourt, Aba, and Asaba remain invisible.

85%+
Of all VC funding in Nigeria goes exclusively to Lagos-based founders, ignoring secondary economic hubs.
